summary: The waiting-queue removal path still left streaming Session._inflight set and exposed queued Mamba requests to normal cache completion with no FINISH_ABORT marker. The fix clears the streaming session lifecycle and installs the initiator's abort reason before any KV release. The regression failed in both reported variants before the change and passes after it; unrelated and committed session state are preserved.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the source fix: 2 failures showed Session.abort_req was never called and the queued Mamba request reached release_kv_cache with finished_reason=None; the non-streaming boundary passed. Raw output is summarized in the PR description.

24 tests passed: explicit queued abort lifecycle recovery, waiting-timeout reason propagation into FINISH_ABORT before Mamba cleanup, committed-prefix bookkeeping preservation, non-streaming isolation, and adjacent streaming cache/session behavior.

The real checkout server loaded the deterministic tiny Llama and executed first-turn and queued-abort HTTP traffic on gfx950. The initial 100-token blocker exceeded the fixture's practical 128-token envelope and the harness aborted before the post-abort turn, so this is retained as non-qualifying diagnostic evidence.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen checkpoint was unavailable, so no semantic or architecture-specific Qwen claim is made.

GPU evidence: reports/j-aa1f4d930390/evidence/http/server.log records the source-checkout server loading the local FP16 Llama, allocating GPU KV cache, compiling Triton for gfx950, and executing prefill/decode plus /open_session, /generate, and /abort_request. This does not establish an end-to-end pass.
No hybrid-Mamba weights were available; the Mamba branch is verified at the scheduler/cache boundary, not end to end on a Mamba model.

The deterministic tiny-Llama HTTP attempt did not complete the final post-abort request because the synthetic blocker/harness failed to drain reliably; its logs are diagnostic only and are not used to label the bug fixed.
Only one assigned gfx950 GPU was used; no distributed or multi-node behavior was tested.
